sentences.text:
Sukhdev Patel S/o Bihari Patel Aged About 26 Years Resident Of Kutela Ward
No. 07, Godpar, P.S Masturi, Bilaspur Chhattisgarh.
 ... Applicant
 versus
State Of Chhattisgarh Through Station House Officer, Police Station Rajim
District Gariyaband (C.G.).

---- Respondent (Cause title is taken from the CIS) For Applicant : Mr. Pawan Kumar Kashyap, Advocate For Respondent/State : Ms. Laxmeen Kashyap, PL Hon'ble Shri Justice Arvind Kumar Verma Order on Board 08/01/2025 1.
Heard Mr. Pawan Kumar Kashyap, counsel for the applicant and Ms. Laxmeen Kashyap, PL for the State-Respondent.
2. In compliance of Court's order dated 21.10.2024, today victim is appeared along with her father before this Court through video conferencing from the DLSA- Gariyaband (C.G.).

On being asked,
she has no objection to release the applicant on bail.

3. The applicant has been preferred this first bail application under Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023 for grant of regular bail as he is arrested in connection with Crime No.205/2023, registered at Police Station- Rajim, District Gariyaband (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

4. Brief facts of this case are that, on the date of incident, the complainant has made missing report to the Police Station Rajim against unknown person that the prosecutrix was gone to any place from her house without any information given to her parents, but she did not return in the house and no any information has received about the prosecutrix to her relatives.

On the basis of said complaint,
police has registered the case against unknown persons for the offence under Section 363 of I.P.C.
and after recovered the prosecutrix, the police has registered the offence punishable under Sections Sukhdev Patel vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29875710/
1 363, 366, 376 (2) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 06 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 against the present applicant.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant contended that, the present applicant is innocent he has not committed any offence, he has been falsely implicated in the aforesaid case.

He further contended that the prosecutrix was love affairs with the applicant and she did not raise any alarm against commission of offence and as per allegation made by the prosecution, the prosecutrix went to any place from her house without any information and she did not return in the house on time, but the applicant has never been abducted her and he has not committed any aforesaid offences as alleged by the prosecution against him.
He further contended that no direct allegation has made against the applicant because parents has made missing report to the concern police station against unknown person.
He further contended that the material witnesses have been examined in the learned trial Court below by prosecution agency and they have not supported the case of the prosecution and turned hostile.
He further contended that, the applicant is in jail since 31.05.2024 and the trial will take considerable time for its conclusion, therefore, the applicant may kindly be released on bail.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application submitted by the applicant.
7. I have heard learned counsel for both the parties, perused the case diary and other materials available on record.
8. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and further considering that the applicant and prosecutrix are having love affair since long.

Further, there is no evidence available to show that the applicant has tampered the prosecution witnesses, the applicant is in jail since 31.05.2024 and conclusion of the trial may take some more time, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.

9. Let the applicant- Sukhdev Patel involved in Crime No.205/2023, registered at Police Station- Rajim, District Gariyaband (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.10,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 269 of BNS, 2023.

sentences.text:
(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence,
proclamation under Section 84 of the BNSS, 2023 is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 209 of BNS, 2023.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 351 of BNSS, 2023.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. However, this Court hopes and trusts that the trial Court shall make an earnest endeavour to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible, if there is no legal impediment.
11. Office is directed to send a certified copy of this order to the trial Court for necessary information and compliance forthwith.

Sd/-
